claims.text: The driver never reached the booked pickup. The trip's own arrival check reports corroborated = false: the nearest driver fix to the pickup sits 476.59 m away at 08:04:50, far outside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius and the 25 m accuracy filter, and every fix from that moment until cancellation shows the vehicle stationary at that same position. The 08:06:50 'driver arrived' button event, and the 'Your driver has arrived' push built on it, are therefore uncorroborated, and the arrival on which any free wait depends did not occur.

On the driver's own account he was not at the booked pickup. His in-app message at 08:07:10 reads 'I reach already at Blk 215 carpark', while the booking recorded in the trip record is Block 251, Hougang Avenue 3; the rider replied at 08:11:30 'I'm at Blk 251 drop off, where are you?'. The only statements in the chat log about where the pickup was put the rider at the booked block and the driver somewhere else, and the driver never corrected his position before cancelling.

Because the free wait runs only from the driver's arrival at the pickup, and that arrival is uncorroborated by the GPS trace, the wait clock started by the 08:06:55 timer never lawfully began. POL-NS-22 makes the 5.00 SGD no-show fee chargeable only where the driver cancels after that free wait; the charge therefore has no basis, and the rider's claim that the driver 'sat somewhere else, then cancelled me as a no-show' is what the record shows.

Independently of the contact obligation, POL-NS-24 is engaged. The deadline is the scheduled pickup of 08:10 plus 5 minutes, i.e. 08:15:00, and the trace shows the driver still 476 m from the pickup at and after that time. A driver who fails to arrive at the pickup by that deadline leaves the rider liable for nothing, and any fee charged is refunded in full — FULL_REFUND of the 5.00 SGD.

The money is on the ledger and none of it has come back: the fare breakdown records payment_status CHARGED, cancellation_fee 5.00, total_charged 5.00, refund_issued_sgd 0.00 and refund_if_voided_sgd 5.00. The whole contested 5.00 SGD is therefore the sum the rider is owed on a FULL_REFUND, and because the fee does not stand there is no driver compensation to be set against it.

The contact obligation does not carry the charge. The record does show two in-app messages from the driver and one unanswered in-app call at 08:15:20, all before the 08:19:10 cancellation, so POL-NS-23's formal test is met; but POL-NS-23 governs how a no-show is carried out, not whether one occurred, and the message that was sent told the rider the driver was at a different block while she sat at the booked one. The contact confirms rather than cures the failure to reach the pickup.

There is no open question here requiring escalation. Each fact these rules turn on — where the driver was, whether he arrived, and whether he messaged and called before cancelling — is carried by artifacts graded COMPLETE at weight 1.0 (EV-GPS-05057, EV-TRIP-05057, EV-CHAT-05057). The one impaired artifact, EV-ADVIS-05057-01, is a MISSING traffic advisory with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight 0.0; under POL-GEN-02 a missing artifact carries no fact, and in any event a traffic advisory speaks to road conditions, not to where a driver parks.

No elevated confidence threshold stands in the way of a final ruling. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band where the AI ruling is final at any confidence, and neither profile carries a fraud flag — the driver's snapshot records fraud_flags = 0 and the rider's carries none — so POL-GEN-22's 0.95 requirement is not triggered and POL-NS-26 leaves the no-show ruling to the AI.

claims.text: The rider's cleanest route to a refund is POL-NS-23, and it is closed. The driver sent in-app messages at 08:07:10 and 08:14:00 and placed an in-app call at 08:15:20, each one before the 08:19:10 cancellation, and the platform's own derivation records contact_before_cancel.obligation_met as true. Both limbs of the contact obligation are satisfied on the trip record and the chat log, so no refund arises on this ground.

The free wait POL-NS-21 grants ran its full course: it started from the recorded arrival at 08:06:50, ended at 08:11:50, and the driver cancelled at 08:19:10 - 740 s after arrival and 440 s after the free wait expired. POL-NS-22's precondition, that the driver cancel after the free wait, is therefore met on the record.

The ledger carries exactly the scheduled fee and nothing more: a single 5.00 SGD cancellation fee, equal to POL-NS-22's 5.00 SGD schedule, with refund_issued_sgd 0.00 and payment_status CHARGED. Where the fee stands, POL-NS-22 directs DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both at 5.00 SGD.

The rider's fall-back is POL-NS-24, and on the trip record the driver did not miss its deadline: he marked arrived at 08:06:50, more than eight minutes before the 08:15:00 deadline (scheduled 08:10:00 plus 300 s), and driver_deadline.arrived_by_deadline is true. The clause's second limb fails as well, because the driver did attempt contact, so the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit it provides for a driver who does not attempt contact does not arise.

The driver's account is not a bare assertion. Every element of his counterparty statement - the wait of more than ten minutes, the call, the messages - is corroborated item by item by the platform's own telemetry, which records the arrival event at 08:06:50, the wait timer starting at 08:06:55 and expiring at 08:11:55, the unanswered in-app call at 08:15:20 and both in-app messages. On the platform's record it is the driver's account that is supported.

The rider's strongest point is met head-on rather than dodged: the arrival check computed on the driver-device trace returns corroborated false, with the nearest fix 476.59 m from the pickup against a STANDARD arrival radius of 50 m, so the trace does not corroborate the trip record's arrival event - and the trace carries no rider track either, so neither party's position is independently confirmed. If the judge prefers the trace to the trip record on this point, the result is two COMPLETE artifacts, both at weight 1.0 with no cross-source flag raised, in direct conflict on the fact POL-NS-21 and POL-NS-24 both turn on, namely where and whether the driver arrived. The record does not settle it, and POL-GEN-26's answer to a fact the record cannot establish is a human reviewer with the money held, not a refund: escalation preserves the 5.00 SGD fee, a refund gives it away.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the 5.00 SGD no-show fee charged to the rider on 22 August 2026 is refunded in full.

The record (EV-FARE-05057) shows the driver cancelled as RIDER_NO_SHOW at 08:19:10 and the 5.00 SGD fee was charged: cancellation_fee 5.00, total_charged 5.00, refund_issued_sgd 0.00. Two conditions must hold for that fee to stand, and neither does.

First, the no-show fee is chargeable only where the driver cancels after the free wait, and the five-minute free wait runs from the driver's arrival at the booked pickup (POL-NS-21). The booking was Block 251, Hougang Avenue 3. The category's arrival test says the driver is at the pickup only when the trip record's arrival event is corroborated by the GPS trace within 50 m. On the driver-device trace (EV-GPS-05057, COMPLETE, weight 1.0, no gaps, 47 fixes) the nearest fix to the pickup is 476.59 m away, and the vehicle then stays at that same spot from 08:06:50 until cancellation; the arrival check is recorded as corroborated = false. The free wait therefore never began from a lawful arrival, and POL-NS-22's precondition is not met.

Second, independently, POL-NS-24 refunds the fee in full where the driver fails to arrive at the pickup by the scheduled time plus five minutes. The scheduled pickup was 08:10 and the deadline 08:15:00; the trace shows the driver still about 476 m from the pickup at and after that time, so the deadline was missed.

The driver's own message supports this: at 08:07:10 he wrote 'I reach already at Blk 215 carpark' while the booking was Block 251, and the rider replied at 08:11:30 'I'm at Blk 251 drop off, where are you?' (EV-CHAT-05057). He never corrected his position before cancelling.

The driver's arguments have been weighed. It is correct that the POL-NS-23 contact obligation was met - two in-app messages and one in-app call before the cancellation - so no refund arises on that ground, but that clause governs how a no-show is carried out, not whether the driver was at the pickup. It is correct that the ledger carries exactly the scheduled 5.00 SGD, which is why the POL-NS-22 fee-amount referral does not arise. What fails is the arrival on which the free wait depends. The submission that the trip record and the GPS trace are in unresolvable conflict and the case must go to a human reviewer is rejected: the arrival test is the record's own procedure for deciding exactly this question, the trace is complete and unimpaired, and the test has run and returned its answer (POL-GEN-26 is not engaged).

No goodwill credit is added: the driver did attempt contact before cancelling, so POL-NS-24's second limb does not fire. No repeat no-show referral arises: the rider's profile carries no no-show count for POL-NS-25 to read.

Outcome: FULL_REFUND of 5.00 SGD (the whole contested amount), driver_compensation_sgd null, no referrals, confidence 0.9 - the deciding facts rest on complete artifacts at weight 1.0, and the contested value of 5.00 SGD sits in the band where the AI ruling is final (POL-GEN-22, POL-NS-26).

ruling.explanation:
The rider was charged 5.00 SGD as a no-show cancellation fee (EV-FARE-05057: cancellation_fee 5.00, total_charged 5.00, refund_issued_sgd 0.00, refund_if_voided_sgd 5.00). The fee stands only if the driver was at the booked pickup and waited out the free wait. On this record he was not.

The policy's arrival test asks whether the trip record's arrival event is corroborated by the GPS trace within the 50 m STANDARD radius (POL-NS-21, with the category's arrival_test). The GPS trace (EV-GPS-05057, COMPLETE, weight 1.0) places the driver's nearest fix 476.59 m from Block 251, Hougang Avenue 3, and shows him stationary at that spot from 08:06:50 right through the 08:19:10 cancellation. The arrival event is therefore uncorroborated, and the driver's own message at 08:07:10 — 'I reach already at Blk 215 carpark' (EV-CHAT-05057) — says the same thing: he was at a different block from the one booked.

That decides the case. POL-NS-21's free wait runs from the driver's arrival at the pickup; there was none, so it never lawfully began and POL-NS-22's precondition (cancelling after the free wait) is not met. Independently, POL-NS-24 refunds the fee in full where the driver fails to reach the pickup by scheduled pickup (08:10:00) plus 5 minutes (08:15:00); the trace keeps him ~476 m away at and beyond that deadline. The rider is owed the whole 5.00 SGD.

The driver's points are answered. His contact obligation under POL-NS-23 was met — two in-app messages and one unanswered in-app call, all before 08:19:10 — and I accept that; but that clause governs how a no-show is carried out, not whether one occurred, so it does not carry the charge. His claim that the free wait ran its full course, and that POL-NS-22 therefore directs DRIVER_COMPENSATION, fails because it rests on the 08:06:50 arrival tap, which the arrival test does not accept: a status the party sets records only that he set it, and it is uncorroborated by the platform's own trace. His claim that he met the POL-NS-24 deadline fails for the same reason. His reading of the telemetry as corroborating his account is right about the sequence of events but wrong about the decisive one — the platform's record shows a button press and a timer, not a vehicle at the pickup. I decline to escalate: the artifacts are COMPLETE at weight 1.0, no cross-source flag fired, and the arrival test is precisely the rule that resolves what would otherwise be a conflict, so POL-GEN-26 leaves no open question. The only impaired artifact, EV-ADVIS-05057-01 (MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0), is a traffic advisory and carries no fact either way under POL-GEN-02.

No referral is produced. The fee charged was exactly the scheduled 5.00 SGD, so POL-NS-22's fee-amount check is not engaged; the driver did attempt contact, so POL-NS-24's 5.00 SGD goodwill credit does not arise; and POL-NS-25's repeat no-show flag is not reached, the fee not standing and the rider's profile carrying no qualifying count.

Outcome: FULL_REFUND of 5.00 SGD to the rider (the whole contested amount), with no driver compensation.

There is no open question here requiring escalation. No elevated confidence threshold stands in the way of a final ruling.
